response.markdown_report:
At 10% progress, select **bounded title-confusable negative replacement** while retaining recent-terminal/Cloze training. This changes one training mechanism and preserves one BERT4Rec per category. Its benefit remains unmeasured.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** (1) Recent-terminal supervision targets revival of older isolated interests, but cannot identify fulfilled needs. (2) Broad matches outranking direct connections suggest testing finer candidate discrimination; titles provide imperfect distinguishing clues. (3) Electronics has the weakest diagnostic separation: 6.62% negative-beats-positive and 0.7269 lower-tail margin. These training measurements do not establish validation ranking quality. The reported 0.5737 inspiration score supports further investigation, without identifying which component caused improvement.

**Insights from related work.** (1) BERT4Rec [1] supports masked reconstruction and appended-mask inference, motivating preservation of the corrected backbone. (2) S³-Rec [2] motivates attribute-sensitive learning, but does not establish that lexical negatives improve this benchmark. (3) Sampled-softmax analysis [3] motivates competitive supervision; PSL [4] highlights the accompanying false-negative risk. Together these favor a modest replacement fraction over aggressive hardest-negative selection.

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed gap test |
|---|---|---|
| Current intent | Recent terminal targets | Retain recent context exposure |
| Specificity | Attribute-sensitive supervision | Title-confusable training candidates |
| Robustness | Uniform candidate competition | Cap lexical replacement at 8/64 |

Three atomic candidates follow. Scores are Originality/Potential/User alignment/Model alignment/Difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment gives a positive (+) and negative (−) reason.

| Idea | Scores | Critical assessment by dimension |
|---|---|---|
| **Title-confusable replacement** | **4/7/8/7/3** | O: + targeted combination; − established mining. P: + cheap specificity test; − lexical dependence. U: + recent/direct discrimination; − suitability unknown. M: + harder competitors; − false negatives. D: + sampler change; − sparse pools require care. |
| Joint title-token auxiliary loss [2] | 5/7/7/6/6 | O: + task adaptation; − established multitask learning. P: + transferable features; − sparse text. U: + distinguishing attributes; − broad-topic shortcuts. M: + richer supervision; − loss conflict. D: + one network; − vocabulary and balancing work. |
| Bounded negative weighting [4] | 3/6/5/7/4 | O: + focused adaptation; − known objective family. P: + robustness; − benchmark dependence. U: + fewer implausible competitors; − weak specificity mechanism. M: + controls domination; − can weaken discrimination. D: + loss-only change; − scale calibration. |

**Selected algorithm.** Retain separately normalized 50:50 recent-terminal/Cloze losses. Replace eight of 64 uniform negatives with reproducibly sampled title neighbors of the training target, excluding the user's complete training history. Preserve numbers and model identifiers; use uniform fallback for missing or insufficient title neighbors. Target titles guide training sampling only and never enter masked inputs.

This jointly targets **older-interest revival** through retained recent-terminal examples and **broad-over-direct ranking** through confusable competition. It targets measured sampled ranking errors without claiming compatibility knowledge. Compare against a configuration-matched uniform control using unchanged macro validation HR@10, charging both conditions to the shared budget. Deploy one selected checkpoint per category; never fuse conditions.

References: [1] [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690); [2] [S³-Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.07873); [3] [sampled-softmax analysis](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf); [4] [PSL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00163).

idea.description: Test replacing eight of 64 uniform training negatives with title-confusable candidates in each category's single corrected BERT4Rec. Retain separately normalized recent-terminal and ordinary Cloze objectives, and compare against an otherwise identical uniform-negative control.
idea.motivation: Retained recent-terminal supervision addresses revival of older isolated interests. Competition against lexically confusable items tests whether the network can rank direct recent-interest connections above broad matches. Electronics' 6.62% diagnostic negative-beats-positive rate motivates testing discrimination, but does not demonstrate a semantic failure or predict validation improvement. Titles cannot establish ownership, fulfilled needs or exact compatibility.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is an implementation specification for the supplied corrected baseline, whose source is absent from the prompt, rather than executable replacement files. Preserve its BERT4Rec architecture, optimizer and predictor writer. Use one independently trained model per category and one checkpoint per category at inference. Never combine experimental conditions or add lexical scores to inference.

Retain all four category routes. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; all generated artifacts stay beneath the trial directory. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch. Preserve the fixed splits and host evaluator.

Use the specified mixed objective: half the batch contains terminal examples, with targets uniformly sampled from the most recent min(10,n-1) eligible training-history indices. Omit the target's entire future suffix, append MASK to its preceding context, and left-pad. Retain corrected baseline Cloze construction for the other half, replacing every supervised target with MASK. Average terminal and Cloze losses separately, then combine with weights 0.5 each; if one component has no valid targets, use the other and record this event.

Build a deterministic lexical index separately per category from supplied item titles only. Use lowercase alphanumeric tokens while retaining numeric tokens and model identifiers, plus adjacent token bigrams. Fit sparse TF-IDF on titles in the supplied catalog; this is preprocessing for candidate selection, not an independently trained recommendation predictor. Retrieve at most 128 positive-similarity neighbors per target, excluding the target and breaking similarity ties by ascending item ID. Construct neighbors in bounded sparse chunks, avoiding a dense catalog-by-catalog matrix. Freeze the index before optimization. Missing or empty titles have no lexical neighbors. Descriptions and unavailable metadata are unnecessary.

For user u, eligible negatives are real catalog IDs excluding PAD, MASK and every item in u's complete training history. Never inspect held-out labels for exclusions. In both conditions draw a uniform unique 64-item negative set, or all eligible items if fewer exist. When at least 64 eligible items exist, retain its first 56 items. In the proposed condition, replace the remaining eight slots with up to eight uniformly sampled eligible lexical neighbors excluding the retained 56. Fill any shortfall uniformly without replacement from the remaining eligible catalog. In the control, retain the original final eight uniform items. For fewer than 64 eligible items, use all eligible items in both conditions. Use bounded complement sampling and record fallback rates; skip targets with no eligible negatives. Apply temperature-1 candidate cross-entropy without claiming unbiased full-softmax estimation. Gather only supervised features and chunk scoring without changing loss denominators.

Use independent deterministic streams for examples, masking, uniform candidates and lexical selection. Lexical selection must not advance the example or dropout RNG. Retain fixed uniform diagnostic negatives so optimization sampling does not redefine measured diagnostics. Track lexical fallback and selected-item training frequency as descriptive checks; do not tune the replacement count on these diagnostics.

Compare the proposal with a configuration-matched uniform control; the historical 0.5737 score alone does not establish such a match. Predeclare equal shares of the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second allowance for the two conditions, including all four categories, validation, diagnostics and failures. Use the host's existing checkpoint cadence and compare the common completed-epoch grid. Select by pinned macro validation HR@10; ties favor the uniform control and earlier checkpoints. Deploy the selected condition's four-category checkpoint bundle, without cross-condition or checkpoint averaging. Report actual updates and GPU seconds because equal compute can produce unequal exposure. Do not train additional configurations under this proposal.

Preserve ModelView, view.model as the actual nn.Module, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data interfaces. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Diagnostic batches remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B x L, using valid MASK supervision. Treat unavailable review and item attributes as unavailable.

Inference keeps at most L-1 history items, appends the reserved MASK, left-pads and gathers the final nonpadding position using explicit position indices, never count-1. Exclude PAD and MASK from outputs. Verify checkpoint configuration and embedded predictor consistency even though architecture is unchanged. Titles guide only training-negative selection; inference uses the single trained neural scoring function. Lexically similar unseen items can be plausible positives, and title overlap can encourage broad-topic shortcuts. Validation gains and the simulator's qualitative outcomes must therefore be reported separately, without asserting improved compatibility or full-catalog performance.
idea.pseudocode:
Predeclare control=uniform64 and proposal=title8; fix budgets, seeds and checkpoint rules.
For each category, build a deterministic title TF-IDF neighbor index from supplied titles.
For each condition, initialize one corrected BERT4Rec per category with seed 42.
For each completed epoch, run exactly 200 batches:
    Construct recent-terminal and corrected Cloze examples.
    Hide all supervised target IDs with MASK; omit terminal future suffixes.
    For each supervised target y belonging to user u:
        eligible = real_catalog minus set(full_training_history[u])
        base = uniform_unique_sample(eligible, min(64, len(eligible)))
        if condition == title8 and len(base) == 64:
            retained = base[:56]
            pool = title_neighbors[y] intersect eligible minus set(retained)
            lexical = uniform_unique_sample(pool, min(8, len(pool)))
            fill = uniform_unique_sample(eligible minus retained minus lexical, 8-len(lexical))
            negatives = retained + lexical + fill
        else:
            negatives = base
        Skip targets with no eligible negatives; record counts.
    Compute differentiable positive-plus-negative logits from the same BERT4Rec.
    Compute mean terminal CE and mean Cloze CE separately.
    Combine valid component means with fixed 0.5/0.5 weights.
    Backpropagate and update once.
Evaluate using unchanged host validation on the predeclared common epoch grid.
Select one condition's four-category checkpoint bundle by macro HR@10.
Emit matching appended-MASK prediction; load exactly one checkpoint per category.
Run preserved diagnostics with a fixed uniform-negative stream.

originality.positive: Combines title-sensitive training competition with explicitly recent terminal supervision in a small, falsifiable BERT4Rec experiment.
originality.negative: Lexical negative mining and recent-target sampling are established mechanisms; the replacement rule is a heuristic adaptation.

future_potential.positive: A low-cost comparison can reveal whether distinguishing textual attributes justify later jointly trained text representations.
future_potential.negative: Lexical overlap may reflect broad topics or plausible unseen positives, limiting transfer and obscuring the mechanism of any gain.

code_difficulty.positive: Changes candidate preprocessing and sampling while preserving the network, checkpoint format and inference scoring.
code_difficulty.negative: Deterministic sparse retrieval, unique negative sampling, fallback handling and matched RNG streams require careful implementation.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item modeling for sequential recommendation.
Provides the backbone and appended-mask inference foundation retained here.
limitations: Does not establish the effectiveness of title-confusable negatives on this benchmark.
Masked reconstruction alone does not identify current need, ownership or compatibility.

related_work.title: S³-Rec: Self-Supervised Learning for Sequential Recommendation with Mutual Information Maximization
contributions: Uses item–attribute and sequence–attribute relationships alongside masked-item learning.
Motivates studying distinguishing item information under sparse interaction supervision.
limitations: Its attribute objectives differ from lexical negative selection.
Its reported results do not establish gains under the supplied data restrictions and evaluator.

related_work.title: Sampled-softmax analysis (TOIS 2024; supplied reference)
contributions: Provides motivation for multi-negative competition and implicit emphasis on higher-scoring negatives.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal title-negative replacement fraction.
Adaptive candidate selection changes the training objective; no unbiased full-softmax claim follows.

related_work.title: PSL (2024 preprint; supplied reference)
contributions: Examines softmax sensitivity to false negatives and alternative activation-based ranking objectives.
limitations: Does not validate lexical candidates as true negatives.
Its robustness results do not automatically transfer to the proposed candidate-cross-entropy sampler.
